title: Thomas Tuchel: England winning Nations League would be ‘best preparation’ for Euros

preparation’ for Euros
 "We want to have these matches on the highest level to prove ourselves," Tuchel said of the Nations League. Carl Recine/Getty Images 
 By Jack Pitt-Brooke Nov. 16, 2026 2:00 pm EST Updated Share article 2 Thomas Tuchel has told his England players that winning the Nations League next June would be the best possible preparation for the 2028 European Championship.
 England finished 2026 on a high on Sunday, beating Spain 3-2 in Madrid, winning their Nations League group and ensuring seeding for the two-legged quarter-finals in March. Their best Nations League finish to date was third in the inaugural edition in June 2019. Tuchel knows how much it would mean to lift this trophy for the first time.
 Advertisement
 Asked whether a Nations League win could have the same catalysing effect that winning the 2021 Copa America had for 2022 world champions Argentina, Tuchel agreed.
 “It is for me, and for us,” he said. “I saw and heard about the celebrations in Portugal when they won it (in 2019 and 2025). It’s the best preparation that we can have for the Euros. And we don’t think so far (ahead), but it’s just a fact.
 “We want to have these matches on the highest level to prove ourselves and to gain in confidence, and to see where we are, and to adjust our game where we need a bit of adjustment. That’s what this Nations League is perfect for. Yes, we want to win it. But first of all, we need to win the quarter-final.”
 Ben White's England redemption arc Tuchel hailed the 3-2 win over world champions Spain a “statement victory”, in which England dominated the first hour and went 3-0 up before Elliot Anderson was sent off. Tuchel was especially proud of how the game represented progress from the World Cup campaign.
 “We took the next steps after the World Cup, and I’m very proud of the performance,” he said. “It’s a real statement victory. It’s not only just winning, but the way we won today and the way we played the third phase was very impressive. Full credit to the players. You could see the steps that we take between every single match. That’s why I’m very, very happy.”
 Advertisement
 Tuchel promised that having set a new standard with Sunday’s performance, England would not be turning backwards.
 “It’s a full package of belief, of courage, of commitment, of togetherness, of relying on each other and stepping up in this moment,” he said.
 “You also need quality, and we showed the quality today in all aspects of the game, big in defending, in the high press, in the low block, in the build-up, in the set pieces, in the goal, in the duels. It was a complete performance that makes me very proud, and we will not look back now. Go forward and stay hungry.”
